title: row11
live_proof: inspection with a line number in the 3.22.0 tree: fts3SegReaderNext() points pReader->zTerm straight into the pending-terms hash key memory at fts3_write.c:1333. Fixed upstream in 3.37.0
object: the pending-terms hash key memory that pReader->zTerm aliases
lifetime_ender: optimize() mid-scan frees the pending-terms hash the reader's zTerm aliases, and matchinfo() on the same row restarts those readers over the freed term
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: one row inserted inside an open transaction, so the pending hash is non-empty and the scan borrows a pointer into it, then optimize() and matchinfo() in that order on the same row. Built in the fts3 group

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT riscv64-purecap, memsys5 over the case's static arena (shared/run-cheribsd.py --mode nested). Revocation acts on a guest malloc free, and under memsys5 there is none: sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool inside one array the guest allocator sees as a single live object. So a tag fault here is NOT revocation reporting, and since 2026-10-30 it is not scored as a catch either: this arm is judged by the mechanism rule the virtual arms carry in tools/arms.json (catch_causes), under which an access the mechanism did not reject is MISSED however the program then crashes. A SIGPROT(34) si_code=2 at the function host ASan reported (fault_sites) is MISSED with the fault kept in its note; a fault anywhere else is not tied to the defect and stays NO-READING:unattributed. What the rule rests on is the configuration and not a silence: SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP puts every SQLite allocation inside sqlite_heap[], sqlite3_free returns the block to memsys5's own pool, and no free() ever reaches the guest allocator for a sweep to act on. The same harness with SYSALLOC=1 does emit allocator=system revoke=on-every-free on 31 of 33 cases (results/2026-10-29-cheribsd/non-nested), so the revoking path is live where it exists

note: Trigger replaced 2026-10-29 and the defect is now reached. The old trigger auto-committed its three INSERTs, so sqlite3Fts3PendingTermsClear had already emptied the hash before the SELECT opened. Putting the inserts inside BEGIN is necessary but not sufficient: in 3.22.0 no pending reader that survives across rows ever reads zTerm again -- an exact-term reader snapshots one hash element plus a NULL sentinel (sqlite3Fts3SegReaderPending), and a prefix reader is consumed eagerly by fts3TermSelect and freed before the first row (traced with probes on PendingTermsClear, the zTerm alias and sqlite3Fts3SegReaderFree). The read comes from a RESTART instead: optimize() frees the hash through sqlite3VtabSavepoint -> fts3SavepointMethod -> fts3SyncMethod -> PendingTermsFlush -> PendingTermsClear, then matchinfo() reaches fts3EvalGatherStats -> fts3EvalRestart and re-starts the readers built before the clear. Host ASan (shared/run-host-asan.py, both controls satisfied): heap-use-after-free, a 3-byte read in fts3SegReaderCmp under fts3SegReaderSort <- fts3SegReaderStart, freed by fts3HashFree under sqlite3Fts3PendingTermsClear. Swapping the two aux-function columns, or dropping matchinfo(), is silent, and so is any matchinfo format without the 'x' directive ('p', 'c', 'n', 'a', 'l' each measured clean) -- 'x' is what reaches fts3EvalGatherStats. One COMMITTED row is also required: fts3EvalGatherStats walks the table after the restart, and with only the pending row that walk does not terminate, so the first form of this trigger timed out on virtual-malloc and on CheriBSD nested instead of returning.
fault_sites_why: Declared 2026-10-29 from the host ASan reference run on the corrected trigger (shared/run-host-asan.py, both controls satisfied): heap-use-after-free, a 3-byte read of the freed pending-terms hash key in fts3SegReaderCmp under fts3SegReaderSort <- fts3SegReaderStart <- fts3TermSelect <- fts3EvalPhraseLoad <- fts3EvalRestart. fts3SegReaderCmp compares the two readers' borrowed terms with memcmp, so the libc primitive is declared beside the SQLite function, as cases 16 and 17 do for binCollFunc/memcmp and case 23 for sqlite3VdbeSerialPut/memcpy; on the virtual arms the fault lands in memcmp. An earlier form of this trigger, with no committed row, had one reader instead of two and reported the same read from sqlite3Fts3SegReaderStep's own comparison -- the same borrowed term, one frame along. The case carried no fault_sites before, because the trigger replaced on 2026-10-29 never reached the defect.
